questionText:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II.
List-I
(Idioms)
List-II
(Meanings)
(A) beard the lion in
his den
(I) to keep away poverty or hunger
(B) an axe to grind
(II) be badly frightened or surprised
(C) keep the wolf from
the door
(III) to confront a dangerous person boldly and
openly
(D) jump out of one's
skin
(IV) have a personal or selfish reason for being
involved in something
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
All four expressions are foundational English idioms: confronting someone menacingly in their home ground is 'bearding the lion in his den' (A-III); having an ulterior motive is 'an axe to grind' (B-IV); fending off financial ruin or starvation is 'keeping the wolf from the door' (C-I); and experiencing sudden, intense shock or fright is 'jumping out of one's skin' (D-II). This confirms (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
